text:
ACME Mobile (customer): Hey team — we've got a customer reporting that their app frequently drops mid-stream when users switch from WiFi to cellular. They see partial responses from the SSE stream and the client doesn't reconnect cleanly. Happening on iOS and Android, ~30-60s after switch.

Maya R.: Thanks for the report — can you paste a minimal repro or logs? Is this our Hosted API or a Dedicated instance?

ACME Mobile (customer): Hosted API (api.redwood.sh). Using SSE (text/event-stream) for streaming chat. Example client flow: open SSE, get a few tokens, switch networks, then connection closes; client attempts to open new SSE but sometimes gets an empty stream or server sends a single "done" event.

Alex G.: Do they see any specific HTTP code on reconnect? 502/504 or just socket close? Also which LB (aws/alb/gcp) and any mobile proxies?

ACME Mobile (customer): Client sees socket close with ECONNRESET. No consistent http code since TCP drops midstream. Reconnect sometimes gets 200 but zero bytes then closed. Carrier: variety of mobile carriers.

Jordan S.: This sounds like NAT pinhole / idle timeout + TCP reset during handover. Two things to check: server-side idle timeout on the connection and whether client is sending SSE keep-alives/heartbeats. Do you have any server-side request id or session id we can correlate?

ACME Mobile (customer): We add a client_session_id in query: ?session_id=xxxx. We log request_id on our side. Attaching a short snippet from their client logs: 

```
SSE connect -> 200 OK
received chunk: "Hello t"
network switch: WiFi->LTE
socket error: ECONNRESET
reconnect attempt #1 -> 200 OK -> no events, socket closed after 500ms
reconnect attempt #2 -> 200 OK -> got "[DONE]"
```

Maya R.: Useful — can you also grab a server-side ingress log for the request_id around 2025-11-18T10:12? We want to see LB tcp_close_reason or upstream flush.

deploy-bot: New ingress trace created for request_id=rq_8f7a3. Trace link: https://console.redwood/sh/trace/rq_8f7a3

Alex G.: I looked at the trace. LB shows `idle_timeout` then a `tcp_rst` from client ip shortly after the carrier handover. Upstream (runtime) saw the connection closed and processed partial tokens; runtime emitted a final event and closed the SSE. That matches the client's second reconnect that immediately got a done.

Jordan S.: Root causes that fit this pattern: 1) mobile NAT pinhole closes during carrier handoff, OS tears down socket -> ECONNRESET, 2) load balancer idle timeout shorter than the typical inter-token gap, so LB kills the connection, or 3) client retry logic attempts to re-open but doesn't supply Last-Event-Id or resume token so server treats as new session and returns done due to idempotency checks.

Maya R.: Repro steps we gave the customer to validate: 1) Start a long streaming session from mobile on WiFi (send session_id). 2) Wait 15-45s between tokens (simulate slow generation). 3) Toggle WiFi off to force LTE switch. 4) Observe client socket error and immediate reconnect. 5) Capture client and server logs.

ACME Mobile (customer): We can reproduce consistently in field. Any recommended immediate workarounds?

Alex G.: Short-term mitigations: - Client: implement SSE reconnection with progressive backoff and send the last received token index or `Last-Event-Id` header (we support it) so server can resume from KV cache if available. - Client: send small keepalive pings (a 1-2 byte comment `: ping\n\n`) every 15-20s to keep NAT pinhole alive. - Server/Infra: increase LB idle_timeout to > 90s for streaming endpoints and ensure `proxy_buffering` disabled at the LB/proxy layer.

Jordan S.: Also check that our runtime treats reconnects with same `session_id` as a resume instead of returning done. Currently we support `Last-Event-Id` to continue, but for Query param session_id we have a short TTL on prefix cache (60s). We could extend that for Hosted streaming endpoints for an emergency patch.

Maya R.: Can you share a short code snippet we can forward to the customer for the reconnect/resume logic in their mobile client? Keep it language-agnostic.

Alex G.: Sure — recommended pseudo-flow:
```
openSSE(url + "?session_id=...")
onmessage -> append token, update last_event_id (server-provided id)
onerror/close -> wait backoff(ms)
reconnect with header: Last-Event-Id: <last_event_id> or ?resume_token=<token_index>
if reconnect returns chunked tokens, resume; if returns [DONE] and you didn't get all tokens, escalate.
```

ACME Mobile (customer): We'll try client-side pings + Last-Event-Id. Any infra action you can do now?

Jordan S.: I'm opening an infra ticket to bump idle timeout for streaming endpoints in edge config to 120s and to disable aggressive connection draining for in-flight streams. Ticket: INF-1129. ETA for rollout: 4 hours (can be hotfixed to staging then prod).

deploy-bot: INF-1129 created and assigned to eng-infra.

Maya R.: I'll follow up with the customer after infra change and send repro logs. If they still see ECONNRESET during carrier handover, we'll ask them to capture pcap or OS-level socket logs.

ACME Mobile (customer): Thanks — implementing keepalive and Last-Event-Id now. Will report back in ~2 hours after testing on a small cohort. :thumbsup:

Alex G.: If they still hit issues after these steps, ask them to try increasing the SSE keepalive frequency before we change more infra — mobile carriers sometimes have NAT/timeouts ~30s. Also make sure no intermediate device (corporate VPN or carrier proxy) is rewriting or buffering SSE.

Jordan S.: Noted. Also adding a small note to our docs: "Streaming best practices for mobile clients" — include pings, resume tokens, and suggested LB settings. I'll draft and link once merged.

Maya R.: Thanks team. Keeping thread open until customer confirms.

ACME Mobile (customer): Confirmed — after client keepalive + Last-Event-Id, reconnection resumed the stream in 90% of cases during our quick test. We'll monitor more tomorrow.

Maya R.: Great. Marking provisional fix. Will close after 24h of validation. :white_check_mark:
